claims.author: instagibbs
claims.question: whether replacement peers should be validated to ensure they actually do useful work before evicting existing peers
claims.quote: Would we want to do more validation of those claims before evicting someone?

status_by.quote: The replacement peer makes the same claims as every other full outbound peer we connect to while the evicted peer has told us that it will drop our transactions.

claims.status_note: author replied that replacements cannot do worse than peers explicitly refusing tx relay and outlined alternative tweaks

claims.author: instagibbs
claims.question: whether there is evidence on the network that non-tx-relaying peers are a real problem
claims.quote: do we have evidence this is a real problem? ... Can we crawl the network to see evidence of this?

status_by.quote: So the share on Tor is even smaller than on clearnet and the KIT data matches the result closely.

claims.status_note: author ran a crawler across network peers finding ~0.8% advertise relay=0

claims.author: fametrano
claims.harm: the functional test checks for non-eviction cannot fail because a node never evicts the only peer on a network
claims.quote: The "not evicted" checks in the first and third cases of the new `p2p_blocksonly.py` test can't fail.

status_by.quote: I took the suggested test changes mostly with a few edits.

claims.status_note: author adopted the suggested test changes with minor edits

claims.author: Bicaru20
claims.question: whether active peers that do not relay transactions should be prioritized over peers that relay transactions but have been silent for some time
claims.quote: Shouldn't we chose the peer that is active over the one that has been silent for some time even if the active peer is not relaying transactions?

status_by.quote: The last block announcement only decides between peers of the same kind. A tx relaying peer that stays silent is still handled by the chain sync and stale tip logic

claims.status_note: author explained last block announcement only arbitrates among peers of the same kind and stale tip logic handles silent peers

claims.author: Bicaru20
claims.quote: I think it would be good to add a new test case here to check that a replecemnt is requested even when the candidate with `m_relays_txs=false` cannot be evicted yet because it is younger than MINIMUM_
claims.request: add a test case to denialofservice_tests checking that a replacement is requested even when the candidate peer cannot be evicted yet because it is younger than MINIMUM_CONNECT_TIME

status_by.quote: I added a check for this but it could be done simpler than you suggested because the test already passes through this state so I added just the check in the right place.

claims.status_note: author added a check in denialofservice_tests where the test already passed through that state
